text:
Mina Patel: heads-up — canary rolled at 12:03 UTC. After the autotune decision the cluster flipped kernel choices for mid-length requests and we're seeing perf regressions for sequence lengths in the ~400–800 token band. p50 looks fine, p95 +18ms, p99 +42ms, and throughput down ~12% on the canary group.

Zach Liu: ugh. which kernel got chosen and what's the routing heuristic? flame graphs + logs?

Mina Patel: profiler snapshot attached (summary):
```
# profile summary (aggregate of 200 requests, seq=512)
chosen_kernel: decoder_kernel_v2 (autotune)
previous_kernel: fused_prefill_v1
cycles/chunk: 1.8e6 -> 2.6e6
memory_bw_util: 62% -> 89%
kv_access_latency_ms: 0.8 -> 3.4  # spike during first decode iteration
```
Looks like the autotuner favored a decoder-optimized kernel that assumes warm KV and different memcopy pattern. Our traces show a KV miss spike at t=0 for many requests.

Raj Gupta: could be an architecture-aware misclassification — we've seen Ampere vs Hopper heuristic differences bite us before. The autotune rules use occupancy + seq len + batch shape; if occupancy calc is off (tensor cores vs fp32 fallback) it could prefer decoder_kernel_v2 incorrectly.

Sarah Kim: routing note: current bucket thresholds are: [0-128, 129-512, 513-2048]. That 513 boundary is pretty blunt. For workloads that spike around 400–700 we should consider a narrower mid bucket (e.g., split at 384/640) or add a short-circuit in the router to prefer prefill path when KV-warm_fraction < 0.6.

Mina Patel: quick router tweak I pushed to canary (force prefill for seq 384–768 while we investigate):
```
router:
  buckets: [0-128,129-383,384-768,769-2048]
  short_circuit:
    condition: kv_warm_fraction < 0.6
    action: prefer_prefill
```
Deployed to 5% nodes.

runtime-bot: canary rollout started at 2026-03-15T12:07:00Z -> 5% of capacity.

Zach Liu: can you also run a targeted perf-ci bench? `perf-ci run --bench=decode-path --seq=512 --nodes=ampere,hopper` and attach flame graphs.

perf-ci: started job 2830001250 (bench=decode-path, seq=512). ETA ~3m.

Mina Patel: perf-ci initial results: decoder_kernel_v2 median latency 140ms (seq512) vs fused_prefill_v1 92ms. KV hit-rate unchanged overall, but microtrace shows cold-KV at first decode step for ~35% of requests.

Raj Gupta: that aligns with hypothesis: kernel_v2 gets better once KV warmed (different memory layout + lower per-step overhead), but for cold-KV it pays a big latency tax. Autotune must incorporate KV-warm_frac as a first-class signal.

Sarah Kim: agreed. Proposed action list: 1) revert autotune decision for 384–768 to fused_prefill_v1 (fast rollback), 2) add a KV-warm_fraction telemetry metric to autotuner inputs, 3) expand architecture-specific tests (Ampere/Hopper) in autotune CI, 4) run longer tail experiments to validate. Who takes the PR?

Mina Patel: I'll open the PR for revert + telemetry. Will include test vectors and the perf-ci artifacts. @Zach can you add the flame graphs to the PR? :thumbsup:

Zach Liu: on it. I'll attach flame graphs and an explanatory section about occupancy heuristics. Also will add a small reproducer that hits cold-KV heavy paths.

perf-ci: job 2830001250 complete. Artifacts: flame_graph_ampere.svg, flame_graph_hopper.svg, microtrace_seq512.log.

Mina Patel: initial canary numbers after the short-circuit change look better — p99 down ~30ms vs bad canary, throughput recovering. Leaving canary at 5% while PR lands.

Raj Gupta: thanks all. follow-ups: autotune: add KV-warm_fraction to scoring, add conservative fallback for band [384–768] if mem_bw_util > 80% or kv_miss_rate > 20%.

Sarah Kim: scheduling note: we'll run a full matrix of seq lengths + batch shapes on Hopper next Tue. I'll put it on the eng-runtime calendar.

Mina Patel: PR created: r/runtime#5421 — revert kernel pick for mid-band + kv telemetry. Setting blocking label until additional telemetry lands.

Zach Liu: ack, will review today.

Mina Patel: final note — interesting root cause lesson: autotune's kernel score was too reliant on steady-state assumptions (warm KV). For workloads with frequent short-lived sessions, that bias is harmful. We should add cold-warm blinding in autotune simulations.

Sarah Kim: agreed. Good catch and quick mitigation.

Mina Patel: closing loop once PR merges and canary reaches 25%.
